title: The Doctrine of The Trinity
paragraphs: Repeat after me: The mystery of the Trinity. I would like to begin this session with some observations that we need to put our minds as human beings in the right frame. The biggest mistake any human being can make is believing that he does not make mistakes. We must accept the fact that being human necessarily means that we will make mistakes. There is another phrase I would like you to write down: Man’s ignorance lies in his belief that he knows everything.

The more a person believes that he knows everything, the more he reveals his ignorance. Write this phrase down; it might be useful. The greatest misconception about man is his belief that he understands everything. In fact, the greatness of creation, the reality of our existence, the reality of life itself, and the nature of the universe constantly remind us of the limits of our understanding. The mere fact that we are alive is a challenge.

Scientific discoveries, for example, constantly remind scientists of their ignorance. Every time they discover something new, it is because they did not know it before. Sometimes science is so impressed with itself that it thinks it knows more than it discovers. But as you can see, I have come to a conclusion, and I have repeated it many times, which is this: all you know is what you have learned. And what I have learned is not all that can be known.

Therefore, no matter how much you know, you will still know nothing. In fact, most of us are guilty of buying books without reading them. We have libraries that know more than we do, and they write in our homes. We are victims of the accusation whenever we look at our books because we have not read them. All we know is what we have learned so far. I am certain that what you do not know is far greater than what you have learned.

Therefore, we essentially live with a tiny fraction of the information that life provides us. This fact means that most, if not all, humans live from a position of ignorance. The unknown is far greater than the known. Therefore, the vastness of the unknown magnifies our limitations. I would like to repeat this phrase. The vastness of the unknown magnifies our limitations. In other words, our knowledge is so limited that what we don't know always outweighs what we do know.

On February 26, 1996, I was holding Time magazine in my hands. This magazine was published in February 1996, that is, on the twenty-sixth of February. At the top of the page, there is a main article entitled "Man versus Machine". On page 60 of Time magazine this week, a story was published about a chess match between a man and a computer. The computer's name is "Deep Blue," and the man's name is Mr. Garry Kasparov.

Garry Kasparov is the world's number one chess player, and he has defeated all the world champions in this game. I would like to quote from this story, as it is an interesting story. Its subtitle is: "Kasparov wrestles with a machine, and civilization is at stake." I would like to quote some phrases from the article. Here's what it said: The article quotes Garry Kasparov, the world's best chess player, as quoted by Time magazine: "He is probably the best chess player of all time.

He sat down in front of a machine, an IBM computer called Deep Blue, and lost." You might think it's not a big deal, but the rest of the story is as follows: The article says that Mr. Kasparov was extremely frustrated. This is what his chess coach told him. He felt depressed because the machine won. It was said that the Deep Blue computer was capable of seeing 200 million positions per second. While the average person can only see one position per second. Mr.

Garry Kasparov, on the other hand, was able to see two, or at least three, positions per second. In other words, the computer's movement outpaced his movement by 200 to two positions per second. What is the point of that? Here is a quote from the article: " Deep Blue's comprehensive knowledge will make him capable of anything." What they are saying now is that this machine knows so much and can calculate so quickly that it surpasses the humans who created it. That's the idea.

It thinks faster and calculates more alternatives than the human mind that created it. Friends, we are about to face a serious matter. Here's what Kosper said: "The quantity of Deep Blue has turned into quality." In other words, this machine operates so fast that it has developed a quality of thinking. In other words, the cognitive capabilities of the machine separated it from understanding the human mind and its ability to calculate. How scary! Why am I telling you this story?

Because humans always think they are very intelligent. Even the machine he created has now surpassed him. What I mentioned earlier regarding our ignorance and limitations, even in overcoming a machine and knowing everything, shows that the human mind is limited in its ability to understand all matters of life and existence. We are limited. Therefore, we must be careful when we conclude that we know and understand everything. There are things that are difficult to understand, that the human mind cannot comprehend.

I think you agree with me. In fact, there are natural things that we do not understand because of their depth. What do we call these things that are beyond our ability to understand? King David said, “I will not occupy myself with things beyond my strength.” This is what David said in the Book of Psalms. The Apostle Paul said in his letter to the Romans, chapter 11 (note verses 33 and 34): “Oh, the depth and riches of the wisdom and knowledge of God!”

How far removed are His judgments from understanding, and how difficult are His methods to comprehend! Who has known the mind of the Lord, and who has been his counselor? Paul says: “How do you know God and his wisdom?” Again, in 1 Corinthians, chapter 2, note verses 11 and 14, Paul says: “Likewise, no one knows the thoughts of God except the Spirit of God. The person who does not have the Spirit of God does not receive the things that are from the Spirit of God, for they are foolishness to him.”

Everyone is saying it's ignorance. He cannot understand it because it is perceived spiritually. Everyone is talking about discrimination. Say it out loud. Say it a little louder. Tell it to our friends on TV. As you know, the Bible says that the only way to understand what God teaches is through discernment, not through university study. This is correct. Studying philosophy will not give you a revelation. I want you to write a phrase.

In the book of Jeremiah, chapter 33, verse 2, Jeremiah quotes something he heard from God. Here's what she says. A powerful verse: “Call upon me, and I will answer you,” says the Lord; “I will tell you things too great to comprehend.” Let me read it again. It is a great sign. God says: “Call upon Me and I will answer you, and I will show you great things that you cannot comprehend.” No matter how much you study, there are things you cannot know that only God knows.

So, the question is: how do we know what God knows? Jesus said in the Gospel of John, chapter 16, make a note of it in your notes. In verse 12, Jesus said, “I want to tell you many things, but you cannot bear them.” Now, what does he mean? Here is God incarnate, walking on two feet, talking to humans like you. He says, "I have a lot to tell you, but I'd tire your minds if I tried." In other words, everything we know about Jesus and what he said is not everything he knew.

What he told us still amazes us after two thousand years. In fact, there are sayings of Jesus that still baffle the greatest philosophers of our time. He did not tell them everything he knew. Let us all pray. He is a great God. He says, "Look, if I told you what I know, you wouldn't be able to bear it. You would be stunned. Your minds would be shocked." The point here is that I should make some things easier for you. I should tell you about it when you are able to understand it.

And in the next line he says: “But when he, the Spirit of truth, comes, he will guide you into all truth.” There are things that Jesus left for the Holy Spirit to tell you because you could not understand them directly from the Word. Hallelujah. He said, " After I leave, I will send the guide, and he will give you more information." He will reveal the things you said and you will see that what you said is not what you heard. Hallelujah. God says that He has information that the human mind cannot comprehend.

That's why even computers are capable of wiping us out. Why am I saying this? Because when we talk about the Trinity, people think we are able to explain it. But we cannot explain the mysteries of God. It is no wonder that God had mercy on us and said that He would not reveal to us everything He knows. Therefore, we see that the limits of our understanding must give way to spiritual discernment if we are to understand, know, and reveal God’s wisdom. This is what is called revelation. Write this down.

Definition of revelation. What is revelation? Revelation is what God decides and wants to tell us. Let me repeat it. It's a simple fact. Revelation is what God decides and wants us to know. This is the revelation. Unless God himself allows you to understand something, all you have is information. The information is not true. Revelation is the truth. Therefore, revelation comes only from God.

That is why Paul wrote in the Epistle to the Ephesians, chapter one, when he prayed for God and peace for the church, “I pray that the spirit of revelation may rest on you, so that you may see the riches of his wisdom.” In other words, God himself must give you revelation to understand what he teaches. Now, I want to mention a very important point as we discuss the Trinity, which is: revelation is always a result of faith. Repeat after me: Revelation is always a result of faith. What does this mean?

This means that faith precedes revelation. In the world I grew up in, and which you were a part of, we thought in a certain way. We were thinking: "I'll believe until I see." This is how scientific assumptions work. This is how a non-believer thinks. That's what you and I were thinking. We believed that we should move from vision to faith. But revelation does not work that way. Revelation comes from faith, then we see. Therefore, we must note here that revelation is a result of faith.

Faith is believing before seeing. What is faith? The essence of the things you hope for, and the evidence of the things you have not yet seen. Therefore, the Trinity does not come about simply by understanding it, but rather you understand it after believing in it. It's best if you listen to me today. Tell me something. In other words, you must have faith first before you can understand revelation. Many people say, "I will not turn to God until I understand Him."

The atheist says: " How do you know that there is a God? I cannot believe in someone I do not see or for whose existence I have no proof." Okay, let's read what the Bible says about faith and revelation. Hebrews 11:6 says: “ Whoever comes near to God must first believe that he exists.” "Here we have a problem. An atheist can't prove God doesn't exist unless they first believe in Him. And that makes sense. If you're going to prove God doesn't exist, you have to prove it yourself.

So you have to be sure He doesn't exist. Do whatever you're told and see if He doesn't exist. Personally, I accepted the truth first, then discovered it. But what people want to do first is discover the truth, and then they'll believe. The Bible says, ' Blessed is the one who has not seen and yet has believed.' Why? Because revelation comes after faith. With God and His truth, we must believe first before we can understand.

The doctrine of the Trinity is, at its core, a profound mystery beyond the grasp of the limited mind, and it falls under the category of revelation. Studying the Trinity is studying the unfathomable riches of God's wisdom. In this session, I'm going to try to address four aspects of this great doctrine. I want you to take notes. First, the doctrine as it is presented. We'll talk about how it's mentioned in the Bible. Second, the definition of the doctrine. We'll define the Trinity. Third, proving the doctrine."

We will show from the Bible that the doctrine of the Trinity is biblically established. Fourth, we will conclude by clarifying the doctrine. We will give some examples to try to give insight into this great mystery called the Trinity. Now, I have no reasonable doubt that the doctrine of the Trinity is taught in the Bible. However, it is a doctrine to be believed even though it is impossible to fully and completely understand. I don't understand the Trinity. Well, let me stop here. Listen to me, everyone.

I do n't understand the Trinity. Because if someone could understand the Trinity, they would understand the mysteries of God. So what we have to do is look at it through the glimpses that God gives us of this Trinity. And God does give us glimpses, brief ones, of His great collective unity. First, the doctrine states that the Scriptures teach that God is one and has no other gods. This is very clear in the Bible. There is no God but God, and He has no other gods.

Now, the Bible clearly states that the Lord our God is one and has no other gods. This statement is truly amazing. It says that the Lord our God is one and has no other gods. There is no other God, meaning that God is one and has no other god, and He is He and has no other god. So how then... how do we deal with this astonishing revelation? The first question that comes to mind is: How could God have any fellowship before the existence of finite creatures? With whom did God have fellowship? With whom was He?

If He is God alone? The answer lies in the doctrine of the Trinity. The divine unity is a composite unity, and in this unity are three distinct Persons, each of whom is the Godhead. Things are starting to get confusing. Yet, He is fully aware of each other, and yet they are one. Yet, they are completely different. Confused? Claim. In essence, there was an eternal fellowship before the creation of any finite creatures. Therefore, God was never alone. God was with Himself.

The Bible says: "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God." This was in the beginning with God. The three cooperate in one spirit and one purpose; they are truly one. The Father creates, the Son redeems, and the Holy Spirit sanctifies. Yet, in every action, all three are present and active. In other words, the Father does not create alone, the Son does not redeem alone, and the Holy Spirit does not sanctify alone. What a mystery! The Trinity is an eternal communion.

The redemption of humanity necessitated this historical revelation. If humanity had not fallen, we would not understand the Trinity as we do today. I want you to try to write this down. I have a list of things that will make you exult. First, the Father bears witness to the Son (Matthew 3:17). Second, the Son bears witness to the Father ( John 5:19). Third, the Son bears witness to the Holy Spirit (John 14:26). Fourth, the Holy Spirit bears witness to the Son (John 15:26).

In other words, they all bear witness to one another because they are one. The doctrine of the Trinity is clearly declared in the Bible, and no one can grasp it with human reason. How can we know? Think about... Is the question of the inner nature of divinity only answered through revelation? We, as humans, have no way of knowing what is in God's mind unless God decides to reveal it to us, because we are the offspring of His creation. We are the product of His creative power.

Therefore, He only knows what He allows us to know. You know, I was thinking about how true this is. You can't understand the Trinity unless God reveals it to you. I've been studying other religions for a while now. I've studied several of them in detail. Even in our university studies, we had to learn about many other religions. And it struck me how logically and comprehensibly the innovations and philosophical developments of other religions regarding God are presented.

In other words, Buddha has a sublime, organized mind. You can actually understand it. Confucius and his relationship to the nature of the universe. They have a very organized concept of God. And so it is with the Baha'i Faith and all other religions; their concept of God is organized. But Christianity is the only religion in the world, so to speak, where the concept of God is not organized. Why? Because we have a problem with the concept of God. You see, I don't know if I'm making the point.

When you create a religion, you create a god that everyone can understand. The God of the Bible is the only God that the Bible itself cannot explain. If the biblical writers wanted a religion that would please everyone, they could have invented a god we could identify with. Like the Romans and the pagans and all those who had their gods. I mean, the pharaohs, they had their gods, very specific. They had a sun god and a moon god. You could offer fruit to the moon god.

And when you were angry, you offered food to the sun god, and he would bring you whomever he wanted. Then there were all those who offered nature gods, a god of... sex. I mean, all the gods rebelled. But the Jewish revelation, through which God received revelation of Himself, is still incapable of explaining God. That's why the Trinity is such a perplexing mystery, because God cannot explain what the mind cannot comprehend. That's how I know I worship the one true God. Hallelujah. Why?

Because if you could understand God, you could manipulate Him. You'd better tell me. With something. But God has done something great. He says, " I will give you enough to amaze you, but I will prevent your minds from being amazed." Why? I cannot explain myself to you. Why? I am eternal to eternity. And if I tried to put eternity into annihilation, everything would explode. Therefore, the Trinity can only come about through revelation. What do we know about God? Only what He has told us so far.

It is true that the word "Trinity" does not appear in the Bible. That is true. But it is there. It is not anywhere in the Bible. It is a theological expression invented during the second century to describe the divinity as it appears in the Bible. They tried to explain what it was, and they came up with the word "Trinity." Now, someone might say, "Well, if it is not in the Bible, we should not use it or believe in it." "Okay, let me ask you a question. Did Jupiter exist before it was discovered? Yes.

And who named it? Man. But it existed before man discovered it. Right. That's exactly what happened with the Trinity. It was mentioned in the Bible all along, but in the second century, they gave it a final name. God existed before we called Him God. I ca n't hear you very well. And God was almighty before you experienced His almight. And God was holy before you called Him holy. Hallelujah. And God was a Savior before He saved you. So He was a Trinity before we called Him a Trinity. Clap your hands.

He is a Trinity without our intervention. So we clearly affirm that the doctrine of the Trinity is in the Bible. I want to define it for you. Now, this will be the most difficult part of the message because you can't define something so mysterious. So I will make a humble attempt. It's important that you take notes for this series because you will have to give an answer as to why you believe. And some of you may encounter people who think they know God and can explain Him in a certain way." Wrong.

So, your understanding needs to be clear in order to answer why you believe. The Bible says that no one has ever seen God. It is very difficult to find human terms to express the Trinity and the unity of God. At the same time, the reality and particularity of God's person and the particularity of that person are very mysterious. The Trinity is not, and I repeat, is not the Trinity of God. What is the Trinity of God? The Trinity of God is the belief in three gods. This is not the Trinity.

The Trinity is not the belief in three gods. The Bible does not teach that there are three gods. Christians do not believe in three gods. We believe in one God who is a Trinity in a composite unity emanating from a single unity that is three. Who is the One? Help me. Secondly, the Trinity is not Sabanism. Now, you will come across the term Sabanism when reading philosophical books on theology. Sabanism is the belief in three aspects of God. This means that God manifested in three forms. This is not the Trinity.

Let me explain why not. It could be so. Because you see, if Sabeanism were a term used in school, I would n't even be able to pronounce it. This term was developed by a bishop called Bishop Sabellien. A bishop came up with this idea and said that God manifests in three different forms. The question is, if this is true, to whom was Jesus really addressing himself? In other words, Jesus' prayer would have been something like, "I..." I came from myself and to myself I returned.

Therefore, I want to please myself, so I glorify myself. Therefore, I am in myself.” He didn’t pray because he had a clear awareness of a unified whole, so he prayed: “I came from my Father and to my Father I return, and I will send you a counselor.” The counselor will teach you about me and my Father. And my Father will reveal me to you through the counselor. And the counselor will speak only about me, and we will abide in you. What does he speak about? Help me, Lord.

Jesus’ explanation of the Trinity was very simple for us. Let me give you a list to write down. The Father loves his Son and sends him. The Son goes and returns to his Father. The Father and the Son send the Holy Spirit. And the Holy Spirit intercedes with the Father. What kind of relationship is this? Let me repeat it. The Father loves his Son and sends him. This is what the Bible teaches. So, it doesn’t make sense if he is the same and yet one but distinct.

The Father loves his Son, and the Son goes and returns to his Father, and the Father and the Son send the Holy Spirit, and the Holy Spirit intercedes with the Father. The Trinity, as it appears in the Scriptures, was clearly defined by the anonymous Nicene Creed. This Creed was written in the fifth century. This is what happened in the Church immediately after Paul’s death.

There were many other religions, including paganism, so they wanted to protect the Church from any possible error, while also safeguarding the biblical doctrine of the Trinity. They formulated what they called the Antonine Creed in the fifth century AD. I want to read this to you. I want you to ask the Lord to grant you wisdom, because this is very profound. I am going to read something I don't understand. Are you ready?

Here is the definition of the Trinity: We worship one God in Trinity, and the Trinity in unity, without confusing the Persons or separating the Essence. For the Person of the Father is one, the Son is one, and the Holy Spirit is one. But the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit are one Godhood, equal in glory, equal in eternal majesty. He is the same with the Father as with the Son and the Holy Spirit. The Father is uncreated. The Son is uncreated. The Holy Spirit is uncreated. The Father is great.

The Son is great. The Holy Spirit is great. The Father is eternal. The Son is eternal. The Holy Spirit is eternal. Yet, they are not three eternal beings, but one eternal being. Therefore, there are not three. Uncreated beings, yet three great ones, or rather one uncreated being and one great being in the same way. The Father is omnipotent, the Son is omnipotent, and the Holy Spirit is omnipotent. Thus, the Father is God, the Son is God, and the Holy Spirit is God. Yet, there are not three gods, but one God.

Thus, the Father is Lord, the Son is Lord, and the Holy Spirit is Lord. Yet, there are not three lords, but one Lord, because we are obliged, by virtue of Christian diversity, to acknowledge each person individually as God and Lord. Therefore, it is forbidden for us to say that there are three gods or lords. The Father was not created from nothing, nor was He created or begotten. The Son was not created from nothing, nor was He created, but the Father alone set the Son free.

The Son was not created or made, but was begotten. The Holy Spirit is from the Father, and the Son, who was not made, nor created, nor begotten, but proceeds from the Father. Therefore, there is only one Father, not three Fathers, one Son, not three Sons, and one Spirit One Holy Spirit, not three Holy Spirits. In this Trinity, there is neither first nor last, neither greater nor lesser, but the three eternal Persons are equal in essence.

Therefore, as was said previously about unity and the Trinity, it is the Trinity and unity that should be worshipped. End of quote. This is the definition of the Trinity. However, it has not been properly understood. We do not worship three gods. We worship one eternal God, equal in essence, distinct yet at the same time the same. There is neither first nor last, neither higher nor lower. The revelation of the Trinity exists only in the mind of God.

When we learn of it, it is because He has shown us a glimpse of Himself. In the Old Testament, the Trinity was not taught explicitly and directly. The reason is quite clear. Here is why. It is mentioned in the Old Testament, but the prophets did not teach it. In a world where the worship of multiple gods was common, it was absolutely essential that God establish in the minds of the Israelites the truth that God is one and has no partner.

Remember that the pagans worshipped There were many different gods, and God did not want His people to go astray. Therefore, He continued to teach them throughout the Old Testament that there is only one God. The God of Israel is one. However, in the New Testament, God presents Himself as a Trinity. The name of God is Elohim. Elohim is a plural word meaning the One who is many. Let us all say Elohim. In Joshua 24:18, the word is used to refer to the one God who is also many. Yahweh is one, and He is Elohim.

Many in one. Genesis 35:7. Read it when you have time. Each member of the Trinity is mentioned in the Old Testament. In Isaiah 63:1-16, the Father is mentioned, and in Psalm 145:6-7, the Son of Yahweh is mentioned. Then, in Jeremiah 23:5 and Isaiah 9:6, Christ is described with divine titles. In Genesis 1:2 and Isaiah In 11:2, the Holy Spirit is mentioned. The New Testament also speaks of the Trinity, but in much clearer and more explicit terms than the Old Testament.

In the early church, they faced two truths they had to deal with: that God is one, and that the Father is God, the Son is God, and the Holy Spirit is God. The early church had to deal with this in the same way it had in the Old Testament. These two truths constitute the Trinity: one God, the Father is God, the Son is God, and the Holy Spirit is God, and they are one God. The only conclusion was that divinity is a real but subtle distinction of personhood.

This distinction was manifested in God's work of redeeming humanity. Now, I want to read you some verses quickly. Please write these down. Matthew, chapter 3, verses 16-17. When Jesus was baptized, he came up out of the water. At that moment heaven was opened, and he saw the Holy Spirit of God descending like a dove, and it rested on him. And he heard a voice from heaven saying, “ This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.” Joy.” Here we have three distinct persons interacting.

We have the Son in the water, the Holy Spirit descending, and the Father speaking. Matthew 28:1-19: “Go therefore into all the world and preach the gospel, making disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.” John 14:1-16: “And I will ask the Father, and he will give you another Advocate to be with you forever—the Spirit of truth.” We find the Son saying, “Ask the Father to send you another Advocate.” All three are God.

Yet they do not see themselves as three gods, but as one. In fact, we read this morning when Jesus announced his destination. He is returning to the Father. One of the disciples asked him, “Show us the Father.” He replied, “How long have I been with you?” What a perplexing answer! But wait. You said you were going to him. Yes. And you are with him now. Whoever has seen me has seen the Father. Yet the Father and the Son are distinct. Don't question me. Just believe.

Then he says, "And I and the Father will send you another guide, who will be with you forever, teaching and instructing you into all truth." "(John 14: 1-17). The world cannot accept it." But the Holy Spirit is not like that; he does not see him nor know him, but you know him, for he is with you and will be in you. "I want to emphasize the word 'He' in verse 17. It's a very important word in John 14. Many people think the Holy Spirit is a cloud, or a mist, or a feeling, or a mood.

They think it's some kind of strange apparition that enters a room and makes people do things. No. Jesus said of the Holy Spirit that He is a person, a person. And he says the world can't accept what? Him. And the world can't see Him. But you know Him. You can know Him. You can't know a cloud. You can't know a mysterious mind in the vastness of space. You can't accompany a mere apparition or something mysterious. No, He says the Holy Spirit is a person.

Look at verse 26: 'But the Advocate, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, will teach you all things and will remind you of everything I have said to you.'" He will have a job. "What needs to be done. He's working today, right now. He's trying to help you understand what I'm trying to say. In 2 Corinthians 13:14, he says, 'The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with you.' He's saying that all three will be with you.

In Galatians 4:6, pay attention. Because you are children, God the Father has sent the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, and the Spirit calls out, ' Father.' In Ephesians 2:18, this is very important. It says, 'For through him we all have a way to the Father by the Spirit.' This is interesting. The Bible says in Ephesians 2:18, ' Through Jesus Christ the Son, we have a way to the Father by the Holy Spirit.'

And in 1 Peter 1:2, ' Those chosen according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, through sanctification by the Holy Spirit, to obey Christ, sprinkled with his blood.' We understand the Trinity clearly in this verse. It says that we were chosen by the foreknowledge of God the Father." The former, by the sanctification of the Holy Spirit, to obey Jesus Christ through his blood, the Son.

In Ephesians 1: 3: “Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us in the heavenly places with spiritual blessings.” In Hebrews 9:14: “ Your Bible study is now complete.” Now, how much more so the blood of Jesus Christ, who offered himself unblemished to God by the Holy Spirit to cleanse our consciences, so that we may serve God! Each of these three holds the same titles and authority in the Bible. And they are all distinct persons. They are the same. I know you're confused.

This isn't confusion, it's a mystery. So I'm going to give you a list of their titles. This will help you. Here is a list of the titles of the three Persons of the Trinity. Each is Creator. They all say Creator. (Job 33:4, Isaiah 44:24). Each is Jehovah. The Holy Spirit is called Jehovah. Jesus Christ is called Jehovah. And the Father is called Jehovah. ( Deuteronomy 6:4, Jeremiah 23:6, Ezekiel 8:1). Each is called Lord. They all say Lord. This is found in Romans 10:12, Luke 2:11, Luke 1 Corinthians 3:18.

Each is called the God of Israel. The Son is called The God of Israel. The Holy Spirit is called the God of Israel, and the Father is called the God of Israel. This is found in Matthew 15:31, Luke 1:12, 6, and Samuel 23:2-3. Each of them is called omnipotent. What a revelation! And each of them is called omniscient. This is amazing to me. The Son is called omniscient. This means He can be everywhere at once. The Holy Spirit is called omniscient. He can be everywhere at once. And the Father is called omniscient.

Jeremiah 23:4, Ephesians 1:2, Psalm 139: 7. Each of them is called the source of life. They all said the source of life. They all give life. Deuteronomy 30:20, Colossians 3:4, Romans 8:10, according to the tape. Each of them created man. Each of these people created man. The Bible says in Psalm 103, 100:3, John 1:3, and Job 33:4 that each of them created us. Then, each one of them gives life to the dead. The Holy Spirit gives life to the dead, the Father raises the dead, and the Son raises the dead.

They all work in the same way and have the same titles. They are called the Life-Giving Spirit. This is mentioned in John 5:12 and John 6:33. Another mystery: each one of them raised Jesus from the dead. 1 Corinthians 6:14, John 2:19, and 1 Peter 3:18. Next, each one of them is commissioned for ministry. 2 Corinthians 3:5 and 1 Timothy 1:12. Write quickly enough. Acts 20:28. Please buy the tape. You need to study these things.
